name: EU DORA — Digital Operational Resilience Act
description: DORA overlay for EU financial entities subject to the Digital Operational Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554). Enforcement date: January 17, 2025. Applies to banks, investment firms, insurance undertakings, payment institutions, electronic money institutions, crypto-asset service providers, and critical ICT third-party service providers. Updated to AKSI v0.3 (31 controls, 17 classifications). Key v0.3 additions: PR-09 (sandbox enforcement), PR-10 (memory integrity), RS-04 (cascade containment), PAY-01/PAY-02 (payment controls), DC-PAY trigger for payment entities under Art. 2(1)(d/e). Companion crosswalk: aksi-changes/crosswalks/aksi-dora-pillar-crosswalk.md v2.0.

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: ICT-related incident classification and reporting per DORA Art. 18-19. Major incidents require: initial notification within 4 hours of classification, intermediate report within 72 hours, and final report within 1 month. Competent authorities are the relevant national supervisory authority (e.g., national central bank, financial regulator). EBA/ESMA/EIOPA exercise supervisory convergence. Payment-related incidents (Art. 23) follow PSD2 reporting to payment competent authority.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Competent authority designated under DORA Art. 46 in the member state where the financial entity is established. EBA single point of entry for cross-sector incidents under Art. 19(6). Payment entities also report to PSD2 competent authority per Art. 23.

human_oversight_mandates.description: DORA Art. 5(2) assigns direct responsibility for ICT risk management to the management body. Art. 17(3) requires the ICT-related incident management process to include management escalation and oversight. Art. 15 requires anomaly and deviation management with management body review of outcomes. Management body members must maintain sufficient knowledge of ICT risk (Art. 5(4)). For payment entities, GOV-04 SoD requirements apply to payment policy vs. execution decisions.

notes: DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554) is a directly applicable EU regulation — no transposition required. Enforcement began January 17, 2025. Updated to AKSI v0.3 (April 22, 2026). Key v0.3 changes: (1) PR-09 sandbox enforcement addresses Art. 9 protective measures and Art. 24/25 resilience testing for agent-generated code; (2) PR-10 memory integrity addresses Art. 9 data integrity and Art. 18 incident classification for context poisoning; (3) RS-04 cascade containment addresses Art. 11 business continuity and Art. 17 incident management for multi-agent propagation; (4) DC-PAY classification triggers this overlay alongside DC-FIN for payment entities under Art. 2(1)(d/e); (5) PAY-01/PAY-02 provide payment-specific controls mapping to Art. 28-30 and Art. 23; (6) ID-02 expanded scope covers all ICT third-party artifact types for Art. 28(3) register and Art. 31 CTPP analysis. 5-year retention for critical function records per Art. 12(6); 7-year retention for payment audit records where DC-PAY present. The management body has direct personal accountability under Art. 5(2).
